reviews.review: Fun, does get a little repetitive but the game play still keeps me engaged. Hopefully maybe there will be a different tower at some point to scale up. But it is a good time waster and it doesn't take much to learn and to pick up as well.

an addictive dungeon crawler third person shooter/action game. will update this review once ive unlocked everything in it.

the randomness adds an element of incentivizing you to play with different weapon types or strategies, but it feels like player skill is much more highly valued, which i like in an action oriented game with randomness.

the shooting and melee weapons both feel good. it's quite slow and deliberate, and positioning matters more than anything. i started playing with a controller (dualsense, steam input), but i eventually switched to mouse and keyboard and have been enjoying that more and getting better results (the bug that apparently increased camera sensitivity in platforming sections with m/kb has been fixed, i never saw it). but both methods felt fine.

the traps some people dislike feel like a normal part of a dungeon crawler, so i don't mind them. i guess their damage was nerfed, though. similarly, the consumable elevator keys also feel like a normal crawler mechanic.

this is a fanservice game, but not in the way that you might think. it's not really about looking at girls, but instead about taking out your frustration on workplaces. the fantasy of shooting up the office is recreated down to scattering individual papers. i appreciate that the office monitors to wreck are crt, it's just more fitting.

if you buy the season pass, dont augment the image track dlc unless you want to slowly lose your sanity during a run.

my only critcism so far is to due to unreal 5 and display latency. for whatever reason, loading new floors often (but not always) gives me an extra couple of ms of display lag unless i tab back out and back in, and i can't squash it. but normal people will never notice.

i want the professor to kaizo me
